raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret “introduce our product to a new buyer” as a single acquisition email for a solution-aware agency or network choosing a host for a new show. The email introduces Transistor through its strongest relevant use case: running multiple shows in one account without an additional per-podcast charge. The one next step is to start the 14-day free trial and create the next show.

intent.reason_now: Choosing a hosting platform is an early decision when an agency launches a podcast for a new client.
intent.desired_action: Start the 14-day free trial and create the next show.

raw_plan.reader: An agency or podcast network choosing a hosting platform for a new client or internal show while managing, or expecting to manage, multiple shows.
raw_plan.reader_segment: Network or agency running multiple shows
raw_plan.reader_scope: Agencies and networks evaluating a host for a new show, specifically where keeping multiple distinct podcasts in one account is useful. Recipient-specific ownership, billing, migration and client-access arrangements remain unknown.
raw_plan.promise: Transistor gives an agency one podcast-hosting account for multiple shows without adding a separate per-podcast charge, while distributing those shows to major listening apps.
raw_plan.orientation: Transistor is a podcast hosting platform where an agency can run more than one show in one paid account and distribute each show to major podcast apps.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move from the immediate choice of a host for the next show to the broader operational value of using the same account for a growing roster, then offer a 14-day trial as the concrete first step.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email should lead with the consequence most specific to this reader: a new show does not have to become a separate per-podcast hosting purchase. The multi-show account model is the main argument, distribution explains that it remains a complete publishing workflow, and the free trial lowers the commitment of the next step. Analytics, API details, private podcasts and higher-tier features would split attention from that proposition. No failing status quo is asserted because research shows agencies use more than one ownership model and does not establish that either is failing. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign: Can the unavailable Transistor source page be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: The reader is making a hosting decision for a new show, and the documented ability to carry additional podcasts without an extra per-podcast charge directly addresses how that decision works across an agency’s roster.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the reader manages multiple client or internal podcasts, they can keep the shows as separate podcasts in one Transistor account and publish them to the major listening apps without an additional charge for each podcast.
value_case.mechanism: A paid Transistor account can contain additional podcasts without an extra per-podcast charge. Transistor distributes podcasts to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts and other apps.
decision_conditions: The no-extra-per-podcast proposition applies to creating additional podcasts in one paid account.
Each show remains subject to the account plan’s shared capacity and terms.
The email should describe distribution to the named apps without implying that listings appear automatically or require no submission step.

claim_conditions: Frame the use case conditionally because the recipient’s current account structure and number of shows are unknown.
Keep the multi-show benefit attached to one paid account.
Do not imply that download capacity increases with every added show.
emails.target_audience: Network or agency running multiple shows
emails.job: Get a new buyer choosing a host for an upcoming show to start a 14-day Transistor trial and create that show.
emails.single_idea: The next client show can live as its own podcast inside the same Transistor account, without adding a separate per-podcast charge, and can be distributed to the major listening apps.
emails.felt_need: When a new client podcast is ready to launch, the agency needs to choose a host that still makes sense when the roster includes more than one show.
emails.status_quo: Agencies may either hold one hosting account for their client shows or let each client own and pay for a separate account while inviting the agency to manage it.
emails.mechanism: On a paid Transistor account, the agency can create additional podcasts without an extra per-podcast charge. Transistor can then distribute each podcast to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube, Overcast, Pocket Casts and other apps. The 14-day free trial is the first step for creating the next show.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the reader may evaluate hosting only as a separate decision and charge for each new show. After: they see that Transistor can be evaluated as one multi-show account for the agency’s roster.
must_not_say: Do not claim that client users can be restricted to only their own show’s dashboard.
Do not claim that Transistor provides a ready-made client-facing analytics or ROI report.
Do not claim that existing shows can be migrated from another host without disruption.
Do not claim headcount savings, time savings, audience growth, revenue gains or cost superiority over a competitor.
Do not claim that video publishing, dynamic ads or branding removal are included in the trial or Starter plan.
Do not claim that the download allowance increases for every additional show; plan capacity is shared across the account.
Do not imply that the 14-day trial proves long-term plan capacity or fit.
Do not claim that every agency should own its clients’ hosting accounts.
Do not turn analytics, API functionality, private podcasts, storage or higher-tier plan features into secondary pitches.
Do not make an exclusivity or superiority claim against Buzzsprout or any other host.
Do not imply automatic placement in every podcast directory without a distribution or submission step.
emails.objection: Will every new client show require another separate podcast-hosting charge?
emails.call_to_action: Start your 14-day free trial and create your next show.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Transistor is the right hosting account for the next show and a potential multi-show roster.
emails.next_step_value: The signup starts a 14-day free trial for the reader’s next podcast.
emails.next_step_limit: Starting the trial does not establish migration feasibility, client-specific dashboard permissions, ready-made client reporting or whether a paid plan’s pooled download allowance will fit the full roster.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the multi-show account consequence immediately relevant to someone choosing a host for the next client podcast; avoid generic podcast-launch language, hype and unsupported savings claims.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use short, direct sentences and Transistor’s practical vocabulary: show, podcast, account, publish, distribute and feed. Explain the workflow instead of praising it. Do not add a greeting or sign-off unless the copywriter needs one.
